name: service-opentelemetry
title: OpenTelemetry
description: Server and browser OpenTelemetry for errors, traces, metrics, logs, and named events.
docs:
## Setup

| Layer | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `HttpApiOtlp.layer` | HTTP exporters and browser ingestion routes; includes ServerOtlp |
| `ServerOtlp.layer` | Workers, workflows and CLIs |
| `BrowserOtlp.layer(options)` | Browser errors, traces, metrics, logs, named events and opt-in Web Vitals |

Configure a collector on the server, provide HttpApiOtlp once at the HTTP composition root, then mount the browser layer in the application's Atom runtime.

```dotenv
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app-api
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp
```

```ts
import { BrowserOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/browser';

BrowserOtlp.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web', events: {}, webVitals: true });
```

`BrowserOtlp.event(name, properties?, options?)` and `ServerOtlp.event` are generic stateless emitters. `events: {}` enables browser event export without page tracking, identity state or sessions. The optional `service-events` item provides BrowserEvents.track/page, browser analytics enrichment, and Events.track server persistence including audit-classified events. Use BrowserEvents instead of a second BrowserOtlp layer when enabling those features.

| Browser option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `serviceName` | Required |
| `traces` | `{}`; includes global exception capture; false disables both |
| `events`, `logs`, `metrics` | false; enable independently with `{}` |
| `webVitals` | false; true enables collection and event export |
| `respectDoNotTrack` | true; DNT/GPC gate automatic Web Vitals only, not other generic telemetry |
| Events batching | 30 seconds, 100 records; exportInterval/maxBatchSize/shutdownTimeout supported |
| `baseUrl` | `/api/otel` |
| `serviceVersion`, `attributes`, `headers` | Optional resource/transport metadata |

## Web Vitals

`webVitals: true` works without Events, SQL or `events: {}`. The browser measures document-level LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB via web-vitals; unsupported metrics may be absent. These are not synthetic SPA timings. No URLs, DOM attribution, performance entries or analytics identity/page context are exported automatically. Subscribers are released on disposal; shared library observers remain document-scoped.

Events follow [OTel browser conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/browser/browser-events/) (Development): `browser.web_vital`, scope `krakstack.events`.

| Attribute | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `browser.web_vital.name` | Required lowercase lcp/inp/cls/fcp/ttfb |
| `browser.web_vital.id` | Required metric-instance ID |
| `browser.web_vital.value` | Required OTLP double; milliseconds except unitless CLS |
| `browser.web_vital.delta` | Required OTLP double since previous report |
| `browser.web_vital.rating` | Recommended good/needs-improvement/poor |
| `browser.web_vital.navigation_type` | Recommended library navigation type |

Group by resource and metric ID. Use latest cumulative value or sum deduplicated deltas, not cumulative values. Identical callbacks are suppressed. Message IDs distinguish changed values but do not guarantee collector deduplication. Web Vitals are generic telemetry, not automatically persisted in the application event table.

## Named events

Both event methods return Effects; run browser calls inside the configured runtime. Invalid inputs fail with a schema error.

| Event option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `userId`, `anonymousId`, `sessionId`, `messageId` | user.id, analytics.anonymous_id, session.id, log.record.uid |
| `context` | Flat attributes |
| `timestamp` | Effect DateTime.Utc occurrence time |

Precedence: context, properties, explicit identity options, scoped log annotations. Values support strings, finite numbers, booleans and homogeneous arrays. Named events are INFO OTLP logs with eventName and active trace/span correlation; they do not create spans or persist identity. Server actor annotations come from ActorRequired or application middleware, not AuthMiddleware alone. Client IDs are never proof of authentication.

## Transport

| Concern | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Browser endpoints | `/api/otel/v1/{traces,metrics,logs}` |
| Proxy | Forwards bytes; optional OtlpLogsProcessor for application events |
| Server logs overrides | OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS |
| OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true | Disables server export, not browser collection |
| Shutdown/page hidden | Best-effort flushing; browser uses keepalive |
| Storage/credentials | Configure collector separately; credentials remain server-side |

Generic telemetry generates no visitor/session IDs or cookies. Apply edge limits and avoid sensitive data/high-cardinality Loki labels. Message IDs provide correlation, not deduplication. Package exports: `@krak-stack/registry/opentelemetry/{api,server,browser}`.
